Definition: from εὐνή (a bed) and G2192; a castrated person (such being employed in Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain (state-officer):--eunuch.
BiblicalUsage: eunoûchos means eunuch. In Matthew 19:12, the text says "For there are some eunuchs." In Acts 8:27, the text says "a man of Ethiopia."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that eunoûchos matters because purity is not prudishness; it is keeping ourselves for the God who made us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
